It also adds rules for who can claim the credit, a $50 million yearly cap, and reporting and survey requirements.

For data centers started on or after April 1, 2026, the sales tax break would apply only to eligible server equipment, and businesses would also have to meet set job, power, and water notice rules to keep the break. ID-2026-H758.aiSummary: The bill would change Idaho daycare rules on watching children while they sleep and on how some children are counted for staffing limits. It would allow live video and audio monitoring for a sleeping child if the provider stays close enough to help right away. It would also say a provider’s own children age 5 or older do not count in the attendance total for a family daycare home or group daycare facility when the provider works out of their home. It would take effect on July 1, 2026.

ID-2026-H721.aiSummary: The law changes how public school building plans are reviewed in Idaho. A school district may choose either the state division or a local government to review plans, and the review must be done within 30 days. It also says which kinds of workers can do these reviews, sets fee limits, and takes effect July 1, 2026.

ID-2026-H516.aiSummary: This law changes Idaho school labor rules and bars school districts from using taxpayer money to support teachers unions in set ways, such as dues deductions, certain payments, or paid leave for union work unless the law allows it. It also sets rules for negotiations between school districts and teacher groups, defines terms like teacher union activities, and adds civil penalties for violations. It took effect on July 1, 2026, and applies to certain contracts made or changed on or after that date.
